churn_resistance.rationale: Data access sits behind one module and configuration is minimal, so framework upgrades would touch almost nothing; the aging risks are local: pervasive any at the API boundary undermines the strict tsconfig, and the client-side fetch-and-swap logic plus URL building are duplicated rather than shared.

findings.issue: The API boundary is effectively untyped (getJson<T = any>, TypeInfo.data: any, getMoveTables(pokemon: any)); API shape changes surface as render-time failures despite astro/tsconfigs/strict.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the consumed PokeAPI resources (species, pokemon, type, move, ability) and type getJson's call sites; pages then drop their (a: any) casts.

findings.issue: The fetch + AbortController + DOMParser partial-swap logic duplicates the implementation in app/src/pages/index.astro:99, so a fix (e.g. error handling, focus management) must be applied twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared helper (e.g. src/scripts/swap-region.ts) imported by both inline scripts — Astro hoists and bundles <script> imports, so this stays zero-config.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache never evicts expired entries (only overwrites on refetch or deletes on error), so it grows unboundedly with the set of endpoints touched.
findings.suggestion: Sweep expired entries on write or cap the map size; keep the TTL semantics that make the overlay tests pass.

findings.issue: Route URLs are built inline in every component/template (also EvolutionTree.astro:17, MoveTables.astro:24, types/index.astro:12), so a URL scheme change ripples across files.
findings.suggestion: Add tiny helpers (e.g. hrefs.pokemon(name), hrefs.type(name)) next to lib/api.ts.

findings.issue: The filter query string is assembled twice — server-side pageHref and client-side urlFromForm — with subtly different rules they must keep in sync (default omission).
findings.suggestion: Share one query-string builder between the frontmatter and the inline script (e.g. a serialized constant or a shared module) so both sides serialize filters identically.

findings.issue: A 60 s TTL means the app can serve data up to a minute stale, which is a lax definition of 'live service whose data can change at any moment'.
findings.suggestion: Consider a shorter TTL or a size/age-aware sweep; current value is safe for the harness (the app only starts after the overlay is applied) but is the main staleness knob.

findings.issue: No type-check step in CI: scripts only run dev/build/start, and @astrojs/check is absent from devDependencies, so strict tsconfig errors never fail a build.
findings.suggestion: Add @astrojs/check + typescript as devDependencies and a `check` script wired into the build or CI.

summary: This is a current-generation Astro 7 app: latest major with up-to-date adapter config, verified-current runtime APIs, two dependencies total, and platform-first client code (fetch/AbortController, URLSearchParams, history, DOMParser) with graceful no-JS fallbacks. Data access is well centralized, which keeps framework upgrades cheap. The main things that will age poorly are the untyped `any` API boundary and the twice-written partial-swap client logic, both easy to fix now.
